nu-map/documentation / src/ / ports/

ports/ Interface contracts

Eleven JSDoc-only files that define exactly what each adapter must provide — and what external actors can do to the planner. No logic, no runtime behavior. The hard seam between institution-specific code and the generic core.

Parent
src/
Driven ports implemented by
northeastern/ (NU), generic/ (fallback defaults)
Consumed via
usePort(IPortName) in any component; wire() in config.js
Rule
No logic, no imports — pure JSDoc typedefs + one named export per file (the port key string).

Driven vs. driving ports

This folder contains two fundamentally different kinds of ports that use the same JSDoc-only convention but serve opposite roles:

DirectionWho calls whomPortsImplemented where
Driven (secondary) App calls adapter — the app drives institution-specific behavior out through these ports IInstitution, ICalendar, ICreditSystem, IAttributeSystem, ISpecialTerms, IMajorRequirements, ICourseCatalog, ILocalization, IAIAssistant src/adapters/northeastern/ (NU implementation) and src/adapters/generic/ (fallback defaults)
Driving (primary) External actors call the app — Claude / MCP tools call these ports to read and mutate the planner IPlannerQuery, IPlannerAction src/adapters/mcp/ — Node.js adapters that bridge the MCP protocol to live React state

The eight configuration-style driven ports (IInstitution through ILocalization) are what most developers think of as "the ports." They isolate NU-specific values from the generic core — swap one adapter folder, and the planner reconfigures for any university. The three newer ports (IAIAssistant, IPlannerQuery, IPlannerAction) are the AI integration boundary.

Base interface

base interface
IAttributable
All ports extend this. Defines getSources() → SourceInfo[]. wire().getAllSources() aggregates across all active ports to build the About modal attribution list.

Driven ports — institution configuration

identity
IInstitution
id, name, shortName, storagePrefix, defaultLocale, portalName, degreeAuditName. The minimum every fork must set.
semester structure
ICalendar
semesterTypes[], each carrying a weight (fall/spring = 1.0, sumA/sumB = 0.5). Weight drives all span arithmetic — no hardcoded duration checks anywhere.
credit units
ICreditSystem
unitName ("SH", "credits", "ECTS"), standardValue, fullTimeMin, semesterMax.
gen-ed / NUPath
IAttributeSystem
Attribute grid layout, labels, getCoverage(). Empty grid if institution has no gen-ed framework.
work terms
ISpecialTerms
Co-op, internship, exchange — any non-course block that occupies semester slots. Each duration carries a weight matching ICalendar's semester weights. Empty if unused.
path helpers
IMajorRequirements
fmtLabel() and fmtLocation() — translate raw folder names into display labels for the major/minor selector.
data source
ICourseCatalog
fetchAll(), normalize(), courseUrl(). The adapter owns the full fetch-and-normalize pipeline — PlannerContext calls fetchAll() and receives Course[] already normalized with term history merged.
UI copy
ILocalization
Disclaimer bullets shown in the About modal on first visit. Institution names and legal language live here, not in locale files.

Driven port — AI outbound

driven (AI push)
IAIAssistant
App → MCP server. isAvailable(), notifyChange(context), getSources(). PlannerContext calls notifyChange() fire-and-forget after every meaningful plan mutation. Disabled in config.js pending hosting.

Driving ports — AI inbound

driving (AI reads)
IPlannerQuery + IPlannerAction
Claude → app. IPlannerQuery reads everything (plan state, catalog, audit, prereqs, dry-run). IPlannerAction writes via propose() (user-reviewed), apply() (immediate+undoable), or command() (UI-only). The PlanContext typedef lives in IPlannerQuery.

How driven ports are wired and consumed

flowchart LR P["src/ports/\nJSDoc contracts"] NU["adapters/northeastern/\nNU implementation"] GEN["adapters/generic/\nfallback defaults"] W["wire(overrides)\nmerge generic + NU"] CFG["src/config.js\nexport institutionAdapter"] APP["App.jsx\nInstitutionProvider"] CTX["InstitutionContext\nusePort(IPortName)"] C1["any component\nusePort(IAttributeSystem)"] NU -->|"implements"| P GEN -->|"implements"| P NU --> W GEN --> W W --> CFG --> APP --> CTX --> C1
Port keys flow from contracts → implementations → wire() → InstitutionProvider → usePort(). Components see only the implementation, never the adapter folder.

How driving ports reach live React state

flowchart LR CL["Claude / MCP client"] MCP["MCP server\n(Node.js)"] QA["plannerQueryAdapter\nplannerActionAdapter"] PC["PlannerContext\n(React state)"] IAI["IAIAssistant adapter\n(app → MCP push)"] CL -->|"tool call (read)"| MCP CL -->|"tool call (write)"| MCP MCP --> QA QA -->|"reads live state via ref"| PC QA -->|"dispatches actions"| PC PC -->|"notifyChange() fire-and-forget"| IAI IAI -->|"POST /sync-plan/:sessionId"| MCP MCP -->|"SSE resource update"| CL
The MCP server exposes IPlannerQuery as read tools and IPlannerAction as write tools. The planner pushes state proactively via IAIAssistant so Claude always has a fresh snapshot before any tool call.

The AI integration loop in full

Three ports form a complete two-way AI integration. They are deliberately separate so each can evolve independently:

  1. IAIAssistant (outbound push) — whenever the user changes their plan, PlannerContext calls notifyChange(planContext) fire-and-forget. The adapter POSTs the snapshot to the MCP server, which updates the numap://plan resource. Claude.ai subscribes to that resource and is notified automatically.
  2. IPlannerQuery (inbound read) — Claude calls MCP read tools (searchCourses, getPlan, auditRequirements, etc.) to query the live planner. The MCP adapter reads directly from PlannerContext state via a React ref passed at startup.
  3. IPlannerAction (inbound write) — Claude calls MCP write tools. propose() queues a changeset for the user to review and approve in the UI before anything changes. apply() makes the change immediately and pushes one undo entry. command() fires UI actions only (select a course, pre-fill search) with no plan mutations.
✦
Current status: IAIAssistant is built and tested but is not wired in src/config.js because the MCP server has no public hosting yet. The driven ports (IInstitution → ILocalization) are all fully active. IPlannerQuery and IPlannerAction are fully specified but their MCP adapters live outside the main React bundle.

Reading a driven port in a component

// Import the port key constant and the context hook
import { usePort }          from "../context/InstitutionContext.jsx";
import { IAttributeSystem } from "../ports/IAttributeSystem.js";

function GradPanel() {
  const attributeSystem = usePort(IAttributeSystem);
  const covered = attributeSystem.getCoverage(placements, courseMap, grantedAttrs);
  // covered is a Set<string> of satisfied NUPath codes
}

Components never import from src/adapters/ directly — always via usePort(). This is enforced as an architectural invariant: if you grep for import.*adapters in src/ui/ or src/context/, there should be zero results (except for App.jsx and config.js which are the composition roots).

Adding a new driven port

Only add a port when multiple components need the same institution-specific value and it doesn't belong in an existing port. Four files to touch:

  1. Create src/ports/IMyPort.js — export the key string constant and a @typedef. Add the getSources() method to satisfy IAttributable.
  2. Add a generic implementation in src/adapters/generic/myPort.js and export it from src/adapters/generic/index.js.
  3. Add a NU-specific implementation in src/adapters/northeastern/myPort.js if the generic default isn't suitable.
  4. Add the optional field to AdapterOverrides in src/ports/index.js so IDEs can suggest it when editing adapter files.

The app core, all existing components, and wire.js are untouched. The new port is immediately available to any component via usePort(IMyPort).
